<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

#40826 added temperature-scaled scoring, and #38965 added setwise scoring (`score_extraction_token_id`). #41188 then added CausalLM setwise and threaded `temperature` into `_process_multi_item_extraction_results`, so CausalLM setwise honors it. `SequenceClassification` setwise still does not: both its paths normalize rows in `_multi_position_score_rows`, which has no temperature. A request with `apply_softmax=True` and `temperature != 1` passes validation, but every row is still normalized at temperature 1, so the value is silently ignored.

Example: pooled logits `[1.0, 3.0]` with `temperature=2.0` should score `softmax([0.5, 1.5]) = [0.269, 0.731]`. Both `SequenceClassification` setwise paths (batched and `--enable-mis`) return `[0.119, 0.881]`.

Pointwise scoring and CausalLM setwise already honor temperature and are unchanged.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- `_multi_position_score_rows` takes a keyword-only `temperature` and applies the same numerically stable softmax as the pointwise branch: float64, subtract each row's max, then divide by temperature. The argument is required so a new call site cannot silently drop it. With `apply_softmax=False`, raw logits are returned unchanged, as before.
- Its two callers (the batched setwise branch of `_process_single_item_scoring_results` and the classification branch of `_process_multi_item_extraction_results`) pass `temperature` through; both already receive it.
- Tests:
    - New `test_setwise_classification_temperature` in `test/registered/unit/test_token_scoring.py`. It drives `score_request` end to end through the existing `ScoringManager` fake (only model execution is faked), for both `enable_mis=False` and `enable_mis=True`, with two items that have different anchor counts (1 and 2). It checks every row at `temperature=2.0` and at `temperature=1e-300`. The latter guards the float64 computation: in float32, `1e-300` rounds to 0 and every row becomes NaN. The fake now returns one row per pooled position when `token_indices_to_pool` is set.
    - `test_setwise_score_mixin.py`: the three direct calls to `_multi_position_score_rows` pass `temperature=1.0`.

Rebased onto main after #41188; the source change is now limited to the row helper and its two call sites.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

No model forward, kernel, or pooling code changed; only post-processing of the pooled logits. Temperature-1 results are unchanged up to float precision: the softmax now runs in float64, matching the pointwise branch.

Unit tests (CPU, Python 3.11, torch 2.13.0+cpu, WSL2):

```
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_setwise_score_mixin.py test/registered/unit/test_token_scoring.py -q
```

| Code | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Current main (new test added) | new test: 4/4 subtests fail (rows equal the temperature-1 softmax) |
| After the fix | 61 passed, 29 subtests passed |

Not run: an end-to-end `/v1/score` smoke test against a real SequenceClassification model.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

N/A. There is no performance claim: this changes a small softmax on the already-pooled `[num_positions, num_labels]` result.

## Checklist


- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 check + format, and codespell 2.4.1 on the changed files, versions from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`; the full pre-commit suite was not run.)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: setwise scoring is not documented under `docs/` yet.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A: no model-output or speed impact beyond the fix itself.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
